steps.name: Load and QC counts/metadata, reconcile sample alignment
steps.question: Do the counts.csv (12000 genes x 13 columns) and metadata.csv (12 samples x 3 columns: condition, batch) align sample-for-sample, and is the count matrix suitable raw-integer input for DESeq2?
acceptance_criteria: Report resolves the 13-vs-12 column discrepancy in counts.csv (identify and separate the gene-ID column from the 12 sample columns)
Sample names in counts.csv columns match metadata.csv rows exactly after alignment; any mismatch is reported explicitly, not silently dropped
Confirms condition (treated/control, 6/6) and batch are represented in metadata.csv, and reports the batch x condition cross-tab to verify the stated balanced design
Confirms counts are non-negative integers (raw counts) suitable for DESeq2; flags any pre-normalization or fractional values
Library size and gene-detection summary per sample produced (e.g., total counts, genes with count>0) to catch outlier samples

steps.name: Differential expression: treated vs control adjusting for batch
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) kidney samples in a DESeq2 model with design ~batch+condition, given the two known processing batches are balanced across condition?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design formula ~batch+condition (batch as covariate) on the aligned raw count matrix and metadata from T1S1
Condition factor releveled so 'control' is the reference level and the extracted contrast is treated vs control
Log2 fold changes shrunk with apeglm (or ashr if apeglm coefficient naming is incompatible) for the treated-vs-control coefficient
Full results table reported with baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj for all ~12000 tested genes, sorted by padj
Independent filtering / outlier flags (Cook's distance) from DESeq2 reported, and genes with NA padj explained

PCA plot on variance-stabilized (vst) data colored by condition and shaped by batch produced, to visually confirm batch does not dominate the condition axis and that the balanced design supports the adjustment
Dispersion plot (plotDispEsts) reported as a model-fit diagnostic
Significant DE gene list reported at padj < 0.05 (and separately with |log2FC| >= 1 for effect-size-filtered set), with counts up- and down-regulated in treated vs control

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the treated-vs-control DE signature
steps.question: Which biological pathways (MSigDB Hallmark, GO Biological Process) are enriched among genes ranked by the treated-vs-control DE statistic (from T1S2), after adjusting for batch?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the full DESeq2 results table from T1S2 (all tested genes, not just significant subset) ranked by a signed statistic (e.g., sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue) or the Wald stat) for fgsea
Runs fgsea against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene set collection staged in the reference store; if present, also runs against MSigDB human GO Biological Process gene sets
Reports NES, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (padj) per gene set, sorted by significance
Explicitly states in the report whether the reference gene set file was found and used, or, if absent, that enrichment was skipped and why

Gene symbols in the DE table are confirmed to match the HGNC symbol convention used by the gene-set file before running (case-sensitive check) so a silent zero-overlap failure is caught and reported rather than passed through

plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch adjustment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 13 samples/columns; metadata for 12 samples: 6 treated vs 6 control) with a known, condition-balanced two-batch design (each batch holds both conditions). Because batch is balanced across condition, it can and should be entered as a covariate in the differential expression model rather than requiring aggressive batch correction that risks removing biological signal. Plan: (1) QC/prep the count matrix and metadata, confirming sample alignment and reconciling the 13-vs-12 column discrepancy (likely a gene-ID column) before modeling; (2) run DESeq2 with a design of ~batch+condition to test treated vs control while adjusting for the known batch effect, with shrunken log2FC via apeglm and diagnostic PCA/dispersion plots to confirm batch is not confounding the contrast; (3) run pathway enrichment (fgsea) on the ranked DE result using MSigDB Hallmark and GO Biological Process human gene sets staged in the reference store, to give the DE gene list functional context. No translational/clinical outcome data is present, so no biomarker, safety, or PK steps are included.
